question.text: Fund CAS holds a 12% convertible bond (face INR 1 crore, conversion ratio 25:1 at INR 40 effective price) and a short position of 50,000 equity shares at INR 40. After 1 year, the EQUITY price FALLS to INR 35 and the bond trades at INR 1,020. Under Convertible Arbitrage, which action best preserves gains?

answer.text: Convert the bonds into equity and cover the short with the converted shares
Double the short position to hedge the bond's upside
Hold the bond (earn coupon) and close the short at the lower price of INR 35, booking gain on the short leg
Sell the bond at INR 1,020 and close the short at INR 35

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.2.3 (Convertible Arbitrage), when equity price FALLS, the fund does NOT convert (conversion loses money vs continuing to receive coupons). Instead: hold the bond (keep earning the 12% coupon), close the short at the lower price INR 35 (gain INR 5/share × 50,000 = INR 2.5 lakh on short), and enjoy the bond's coupon income. This is the 'fall' branch of the strategy. The Trap: Option A (converting during a fall) destroys value. Option C adds directional risk. Option D prematurely exits the bond, forfeiting future coupons and the embedded conversion optionality. Cross-Exam Context: Convertible-arb playbook tested in XIX-B and VIII (Equity Derivatives). Manager's Pro-Tip: Set a clear decision-matrix BEFORE entering the trade: if equity drops X%, close short + hold bond; if equity rises Y%, convert + deliver. Pre-committing prevents emotional mid-trade revision.
